Comment: Hedges' g = -0.259 and M_diff = -4.5 were computed from the explicitly reported week-8 unadjusted means, SDs, and analyzed sample sizes. Report_ID: SF-36 mental function score at 8 weeks
Title: Effect of Omega-3 Fatty Acids Supplementation on Depressive Symptoms and on Health-Related Quality of Life in the Treatment of Elderly Women with Depression: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Randomized Clinical Trial
Author: Rondanelli et al.
Comment: The paper did not report Hedges' g. It was computed from the explicitly reported end-of-treatment means, SDs, and analysed group sizes. The pooled-SD Cohen d for omega-3 minus placebo was 1.8529; applying the small-sample correction and reversing the sign to the requested placebo-minus-omega-3 convention gives g = -1.821. M_diff was computed as group_2 minus group_1: 44.6 - 69.8 = -25.2. SE_diff was computed from the reported SDs and n values as sqrt(11.0^2/22 + 15.6^2/24) = 3.955. The reported p value is an inequality (<0.001), so p_value was left null rather than entered as an exact value. The paper's unadjusted difference is expressed in the opposite order (n-3 minus placebo = 25.2).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('n-3 LCPUFA group (2.5 g/day: 1.67 g EPA and 0.83 g DHA)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: 8-week double-blind randomized placebo-controlled parallel-group clinical trial
domain: Depression and health-related quality of life
Topic of Content: Omega-3 supplementation for depression and health-related quality of life
Participant type: Women aged 66–95 years with DSM-IV-TR major depression or dysthymia
Recruitment source: Institutionalized residents of a nursing home in Pavia
Outcome measurement: SF-36 standardized mental component summary score; higher scores indicate better health status
Outcome variable: SF-36 mental function score at 8 weeks

Title: Long-Chain Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplements in Depressed Heart Failure Patients: Results of the OCEAN Trial
Author: Jiang et al.
Comment: Parenthetical values are standard errors of adjusted endpoint estimates, not SDs; they were entered in SE fields. The trial has a shared placebo arm. The paper reports placebo n=28; it was not replaced by the synthesis-plan split n=14 because the prompt's anti-hallucination rule requires numeric fields to be verbatim. Downstream synthesis should split the shared placebo n equally across the two comparisons. No SMD/Hedges' g was computed here because raw end-point SDs are not reported and the displayed values are covariate-adjusted estimates.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('High EPA') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA: missing F-value or group sizes

Title: A Double-Blind, Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial Comparing Eicosapentaenoic Acid Versus Docosahexaenoic Acid for Depression
Author: Mischoulon et al.
Comment: The paper reports adjusted LS mean CHANGE from baseline with SE, not the end-of-treatment raw mean and SD required by the synthesis plan. Values labeled SE were stored as SE, not SD. The F test and P value are the omnibus three-group treatment-by-time interaction, whereas the standardized effect size is the paper's reported EPA-versus-placebo pairwise value. The placebo N is reported as 59 and is retained verbatim; it was not split because the anti-hallucination rule permits only verbatim numeric values and an equal split would be 29.5 rather than a reported analysed participant count.
